title: JC H2 complex numbers: the Argand diagram

scenes.caption: A complex number is a point on the Argand diagram
scenes.narration: A complex number is a point on the Argand diagram. Watch z equal 3 plus 2i travel 3 across the real axis, then 2 up the imaginary axis — the journey itself is the number.

shape.explain: The real axis: the horizontal number line.
The imaginary axis: the vertical axis for the i part.
Re: the real-axis label.
Im: the imaginary-axis label.
The point z: 3 across, 2 up from the origin.
The real journey: 3 steps across the real axis.
The imaginary journey: 2 steps up the imaginary axis.
The number: z = 3 + 2i, a point on the plane.

steps.text: A complex number is a point: x across, iy up

scenes.caption: Modulus is the distance from the origin
scenes.narration: The modulus of z is its distance from the origin. Watch the green line grow from the origin out to z: that length is the modulus. The x and iy legs make a right triangle — Pythagoras: root of x squared plus y squared.

shape.explain: The origin: distances are measured from here.
The point z: the modulus is its distance from the origin.
The modulus line: it grows from the origin out to z.
The x leg of the right triangle.
The iy leg of the right triangle.
The complex number z in Cartesian form: real part x plus i times imaginary part y.
The modulus formula: Pythagoras on the two legs.

scenes.caption: Argument is the angle; the conjugate mirrors it
scenes.narration: The argument of z is the angle its arrow makes with the real axis. Watch the arrow sweep up from the axis to theta. Then it dives below the axis to the mirror image: the imaginary part flips sign — that is the conjugate.

shape.explain: The real axis: the horizontal number line through the origin.
The imaginary axis: the vertical number line through the origin.
The complex number z as an arrow from the origin to the point (x, y).
Theta: the argument, the angle the arrow makes with the real axis.
The argument: arg z = theta, the arrow's angle.
The arrow for z: it sweeps up to theta, then dives to the mirror image.
The conjugate: x - iy, the mirror image below the axis.

steps.text: Conjugate: the same point, flipped across the real axis

scenes.caption: Multiplying rotates and stretches
scenes.narration: Multiplying rotates by the angle and stretches. On the unit circle, 1 sits at angle zero. Times i sweeps a quarter turn to i; times i again lands on minus 1: i squared equals minus 1. De Moivre just adds the angles.

shape.explain: The unit circle: radius 1, where multiplying by i is a quarter turn.
The running product: each multiplication by i rotates it a quarter turn.
The point 1: angle zero, where the multiplication journey starts.
The radius arrow: it sweeps a quarter turn with each multiplication by i.
Times i: a quarter-turn rotation of the radius arrow.
The point i: one quarter turn from 1.
The point -1: two quarter turns from 1; i squared = -1.

shape.text: × i turns 1 to i; again gives i² = −1
shape.explain: The pattern so far: times i turns 1 to i; times i again gives i squared = -1.
De Moivre's theorem: powers turn multiplication into adding angles.

steps.text: De Moivre: multiply the lengths, add the angles

shape.text: de Moivre: powers turn multiplication into angles
shape.explain: The takeaway: de Moivre turns powers into angle arithmetic.

scenes.caption: A common mistake: angles wrap around
scenes.narration: A common mistake: If arg(z) = 100 degrees then arg(z^3) = 300 degrees. The dot hops round three 100-degree turns to 300 degrees, but multiplying the angle can overshoot 180 degrees, which breaks the principal range. Angles wrap around: the principal Arg must land in -180 to 180 degrees, so arg(z^3) = -60 degrees.

shape.explain: Scene flag: an angle-range slip follows.
The angle circle: the dot hops round it in 100-degree turns.
The point z at 300 degrees: past 180 it leaves the principal argument range.
The radius to z: its angle from the positive real axis is the argument.
The first hop: theta = 100 degrees.
The second hop: 2 theta = 200 degrees.
The third hop: 3 theta = 300 degrees, past the 180-degree edge.
The wrap: 300 degrees overshoots the principal range, so Arg = -60 degrees.

steps.text: Angles wrap around; only the principal value is Arg
